cohort: The study included 1,189 pregnancies conceived by in vitro fertilization (IVF), comprising singleton, dichorionic twin, and vanishing twin pregnancies (spontaneous reduction to one by 14 weeks of gestation), all resulting in a live birth at or beyond 24 weeks of gestation.
finding: Vanishing twin pregnancies and singleton pregnancies conceived by IVF had similar perinatal and peripartum outcomes, both of which were significantly better than those of dichorionic twin pregnancies.
followup_time: Peripartum period (outcomes at delivery and immediately before/after birth)
birth_weight: Mean birth weights were 3,207g for singletons, 2,539g for twins, and 3,175g for vanishing twins.
gest_age: Mean gestational ages were 38.6 weeks for singletons, 35.5 weeks for twins, and 38.5 weeks for vanishing twins.
